A1.justification: Both readable 30-page PDFs describe Dynamic Negative Guidance of Diffusion Models and include Appendices A-H. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian simulations, MNIST/CIFAR10 class-removal experiments, and Stable Diffusion evaluations, including additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and outcomes, including the class-removal curves, text-to-image examples, and quantitative results in Table 4.

M1.justification: DNG's posterior-dependent guidance and Algorithms 1-2 are unchanged. The lagged-posterior approximation displayed separately as Equation (13) in v2 is expressed through prose referencing Equation (12) in v3, without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain the Gaussian examples, MNIST digit 0-3 removal, CIFAR10 airplane/car/bird/cat removal, and the same five Stable Diffusion prompt cases. No additional coverage is reported.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: CFG and NP in the Gaussian comparison, NP and Safe Latent Diffusion in class removal, and NP in the Stable Diffusion evaluations.

E3.justification: Both retain the same guidance sweeps, models, classifiers, and evaluation metrics, including FID using 10,240 generated images and text-to-image comparisons averaging 32 images. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The posterior-approximation checks, SLD threshold search in Appendix E, prompt-dependent guidance analysis in Appendix F, and qualitative guidance-strength comparisons in Appendix H are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: The fixed-seed comparison description, image-averaging information, and Table 4 plus/minus summaries are unchanged. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The plotted results, generated examples, and numerical entries are unchanged. Table 4 reports the same average Q values in both PDFs: 0.007 ± 0.014 for NP and 0.052 ± 0.022 for DNG.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds the condition 'in the case of stochastic sampling' to the posterior trajectory-independence identity, narrowing its stated mathematical scope. The Appendix C proof and other derivations are unchanged apart from equation numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free dynamic negative guidance, improved class-removal tradeoffs, and reduced interference from unrelated negative prompts.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly qualifies posterior trajectory independence as applying to stochastic sampling. The existing limitations concerning text-to-image validation, prompt-specific tuning, and reduced user control remain unchanged in Section 5 and the appendices.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters in Tables 1-3, and pretrained-model access information are unchanged. The abstract replaces the printed repository URL with 'this link', but its embedded destination is identical.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and the related-work discussion and positioning relative to NP, SLD, and concept-erasure approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises author, affiliation, and publication-status text, adds acknowledgments, and makes local explanatory edits in Section 3.2. The section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 compacts the title/author layout, moves Figure 4 from page 9 to page 8, and replaces a standalone equation display with prose. Text consequently reflows, while the figures and tables retain their content and designs.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves precision by explicitly restricting the posterior-independence statement to stochastic sampling and streamlining the repeated approximation explanation in Section 3.2. The method and empirical evidence remain unchanged, as do the substantive text-to-image validation limitations in Section 5; the overall gain is limited.
